# RegTrac — full text

Leadership as of 12 Sep 2026. Built 2026-09-12 15:44 UTC.

## Register

### Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Type: Statutory regulator. Statute: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (operational 1 Apr 1935). Established: 1935. Under: Autonomous (within Ministry of Finance architecture).
Mandate: Banking, NBFCs, payment systems (PSS Act 2007), credit information companies, monetary policy, forex (FEMA 1999)
Grievance: RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme — cms.rbi.org.in (free; escalate after 30 days of no reply from the regulated entity)
Site: https://www.rbi.org.in

### Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Type: Statutory regulator. Statute: SEBI Act, 1992 (statutory; existed as non-statutory body since 1988). Established: 1988. Under: Ministry of Finance.
Mandate: Securities markets: brokers, mutual funds, AIFs, listed companies, FPIs, investment advisers, credit rating agencies
Grievance: SCORES 2.0 — scores.gov.in; SMART ODR for online dispute resolution
Site: https://www.sebi.gov.in

### Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
Type: Statutory regulator. Statute: IRDA Act, 1999. Established: 1999. Under: Ministry of Finance.
Mandate: Insurers, intermediaries, web aggregators, TPAs; product oversight; policyholder protection
Grievance: Bima Bharosa portal + Insurance Ombudsman (cioins.gov.in)
Site: https://irdai.gov.in (HQ: Hyderabad)

### Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)
Type: Statutory regulator. Statute: PFRDA Act, 2013 (statutory w.e.f. 1 Feb 2014; interim body since 2003). Established: 2003. Under: Ministry of Finance.
Mandate: NPS and APY: pension funds, central recordkeeping agencies, points of presence, retirement advisers
Grievance: NPS Ombudsman under PFRDA (Redressal of Subscriber Grievance) Regulations, 2015; CRA helplines
Site: https://www.pfrda.org.in

### Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI)
Type: Statutory regulator. Statute: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (Board constituted 1 Oct 2016). Established: 2016. Under: Ministry of Finance.
Mandate: Insolvency professionals, insolvency professional agencies, information utilities; CIRP and liquidation process oversight
Grievance: Grievance and Complaint Handling Regulations, 2017 (amended Feb 2026)
Site: https://www.ibbi.gov.in

### International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA)
Type: Statutory regulator. Statute: IFSCA Act, 2019 (operational 1 Oct 2020). Established: 2020. Under: Ministry of Finance.
Mandate: Unified regulator for GIFT IFSC: banking, capital markets, insurance, fintech sandbox, aircraft and ship leasing
Grievance: IFSCA complaint channels for IFSC-registered entities
Site: https://ifsca.gov.in

### National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
Type: Statutory regulator. Statute: NABARD Act, 1981 (established 12 Jul 1982). Established: 1982. Under: Ministry of Finance.
Mandate: Refinance and development finance for agriculture and rural India; statutory supervisory role over cooperative banks and RRBs
Grievance: Customers of supervised institutions use RBI Ombudsman route; NABARD itself handles institutional complaints
Site: https://www.nabard.org

### Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC)
Type: Statutory · adjacent. Statute: DICGC Act, 1961 (corporation constituted 1978). Established: 1978. Under: Reserve Bank of India (wholly owned).
Mandate: Deposit insurance: Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank per right (since 4 Feb 2020); insurer of last resort on bank failure
Grievance: Claims routed via failed banks; RBI Ombudsman for related disputes
Site: https://dicgc.org.in

### National Housing Bank (NHB)
Type: Statutory · adjacent. Statute: NHB Act, 1987 (established 9 Jul 1988). Established: 1988. Under: Reserve Bank of India (wholly owned).
Mandate: Housing finance refinance and development; HFC regulation transferred to RBI on 9 Aug 2019
Grievance: HFC complaints now under RBI Ombudsman
Site: https://nhb.org.in

### Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
Type: Statutory · adjacent. Statute: SIDBI Act, 1989 (began operations 2 Apr 1990). Established: 1990. Under: Ministry of Finance.
Mandate: Development finance for MSMEs; fund of funds; refinancing; not a conduct regulator
Grievance: Direct borrow customers: SIDBI grievance desk; otherwise lender's own channels
Site: https://www.sidbi.in

### National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)
Type: Statutory · adjacent. Statute: Companies Act, 2013, section 132 (constituted 2018). Established: 2018. Under: Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
Mandate: Audit oversight: auditors and audit firms of listed and large unlisted companies; enforcement of accounting and auditing standards
Grievance: No retail grievance channel — enforcement-led
Site: https://nfra.gov.in

### Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)
Type: Non-statutory · context. Statute: No statute — created by executive resolution, 2010. Established: 2010. Under: Chaired ex officio by the Union Finance Minister.
Mandate: Apex coordination body: financial stability, inter-regulator issues, financial literacy and inclusion councils, cyber security forum
Grievance: No direct public grievance channel; minutes largely unpublished
Site: https://dea.gov.in

### National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)
Type: Non-statutory · context. Statute: Section 8 not-for-profit company (2008), founded by RBI and IBA — not statutory. Established: 2008. Under: Not a government body.
Mandate: Runs retail payment rails: UPI, IMPS, NACH, RuPay, AePS, NETC — as an RBI-authorised payment system operator under PSS Act 2007
Grievance: Escalate: PSP/bank first, then NPCI, then RBI Ombudsman (covers UPI failures)
Site: https://www.npci.org.in

- 1992-04-12 SEBI: SEBI Act, 1992 — statutory powers granted after the 1992 securities scam
- 1990-04-02 SIDBI: SIDBI began operations 2 Apr 1990
- 1989-12-31 SIDBI: SIDBI Act, 1989 enacted
- 1988-07-09 NHB: NHB established 9 Jul 1988
- 1988-01-01 SEBI: SEBI set up as a non-statutory administrative body
- 1987-12-30 NHB: National Housing Bank Act, 1987 enacted
- 1982-07-12 NABARD: NABARD established (12 Jul 1982)
- 1981-12-31 NABARD: NABARD Act, 1981 enacted
- 1978-07-15 DICGC: DICGC constituted from merger of Deposit Insurance Corporation (1962) and Credit Guarantee Corporation (1971)
- 1961-12-07 DICGC: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act, 1961
- 1949-03-01 RBI: Banking Companies Act, 1949 (renamed Banking Regulation Act, 1966) gives RBI licensing and supervision of banks
- 1934-03-06 RBI: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 passed; bank operational 1 Apr 1935

## Scope

RegTrac tracks entities with statutory rule-writing power over India's financial sector: the seven core regulators (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, IBBI, IFSCA, NABARD), adjacent statutory bodies (DICGC, NHB, SIDBI, NFRA), and non-statutory context entities that shape policy without a statute (FSDC, NPCI).

Out of scope by design: self-regulatory organisations — those live in SROTrac. Ministry-level policy making (Department of Economic Affairs, Department of Financial Services, MCA) enters RegTrac only where it touches regulator appointments; the LobbyWatch layer will own it properly.

## Method

- The register is a small, auditable CSV — one row per entity — with the statute, establishing date, parent ministry, mandate and consumer grievance route.
- Leadership rows are added only with an appointment date and a source URL. Claims without a source stay out.
- The timeline is one row per event, same rule.
- Everything is regenerated from data by a single build script; the site is static HTML with no trackers, no cookies, no JavaScript dependencies.

## Caveats

- Leadership positions are stated **as of 12 Sep 2026** and will drift; rows carry their source so the next refresh can re-verify.
- "Statutory adjacent" bodies (DICGC, NHB, SIDBI, NFRA) are institutions with statutory foundations but narrower or shifted regulatory roles (e.g., HFC regulation moved from NHB to RBI in 2019).
- FSDC and NPCI are listed as context precisely because they lack statutes — the most consequential coordination in Indian finance happens in a body with no statutory foundation, and the payment rails are run by an industry-owned company. Both facts belong on the record, not in a footnote.

## The stack

RegTrac is layer one of a three-layer sousveillance stack for Indian financial policy making:

1. **RegTrac** (this site) — the *rule-writers*: statutory regulators, their powers, appointments, consultations and grievance machinery.
2. **SROTrac** — the *rule-borrowers*: RBI-recognised self-regulatory organisations and — the part that matters — their member rosters, where industry consensus on fees and conduct actually forms.
3. **LobbyWatch** (planned) — the *rule-buyers*: who submits on consultations, who meets whom, the revolving door between regulator and regulated, industry-association access to FSDC and ministries.

The stack's promise is the join: a consultation submission on an RBI draft (LobbyWatch), cross-referenced against SRO membership (SROTrac), cross-referenced against the regulatory change that followed (RegTrac). Each layer alone is a directory; together they are a map of how financial policy gets made in India — and for whom.

## Open data

`data/regulators.csv`, `data/leadership.csv`, `data/events.csv` and a DuckDB database ship in the repository, plus an `llms.txt` for machine readers. Take it, fork it, build on it — attribution appreciated.
